sanskrit:
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः।
कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन।।
image_english: A yogī is greater than the ascetic, empiricist, or fruitive worker. Therefore, be a yogī, O Arjuna.
caption:
Chapter 6, Verse 46

Kṛṣṇa establishes the hierarchy of human endeavors. ‘tapasvibhyo ’dhiko yogī’ (A yogī is greater than the ascetic). ‘jñānibhyo ’pi mato ’dhikaḥ’ (Greater than the empiric philosopher). ‘karmibhyaś cādhiko yogī’ (And greater than the fruitive worker). ‘tasmād yogī bhavārjuna’ (Therefore, O Arjuna, in all circumstances, be a yogī). Asceticism tortures the body; Philosophy strains the brain; Work strains the muscles. Yoga engages the Soul. It is the highest because it connects directly with the Source. Kṛṣṇa wants Arjuna to be a ‘Yogī-Warrior’.
